job.title: Technical Product Development Manager - Home Pest
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established consumer products business with a strong presence across Australia and a portfolio of well-recognised brands sold through major retail channels.

With an established R&D and innovation capability, the business is investing in their home pest portfolio as part of its continued growth.  

The Opportunity
Reporting to the R&D Director and working closely across Marketing, Innovation, Supply Chain and Procurement, you will lead the technical development and commercialisation of the home pest portfolio.

Working predominantly through third-party formulation, testing, regulatory and manufacturing partners, you will determine the best technical pathway from product brief through to commercial launch.

There is genuine autonomy. You will bring the specialist knowledge and commercial judgement to recommend the right path, challenge proposals where required and keep multiple product developments moving.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading technical development from brief through to commercial launch
  • Evaluating formulations, efficacy, claims, stability and packaging compatibility
  • Selecting and managing external technical and manufacturing partners
  • Managing APVMA registration pathways and regulatory requirements
  • Driving projects through stage-gate and NPD processes
  • Managing technical risk against cost, timing and commercial requirements
  • Building internal technical knowledge to support the portfolio longer term
The role is offered as an 18-24 month fixed-term contract. Sydney is preferred, with Melbourne, Queensland and other East Coast locations considered for the right person. Travel to suppliers, manufacturers, laboratories and trial sites will be required.
  
About You
You are an experienced technical or product development professional who understands how to move regulated products from concept through to commercial launch.

Ideally, you will have worked within FMCG or a fast-paced consumer products environment, with an understanding of stage-gate development, commercial deadlines and the balance between technical and commercial requirements.

Direct consumer or household pest experience would be highly regarded. Candidates from professional pest control, crop protection or related chemical sectors will also be considered where they bring strong product commercialisation experience.

To succeed, you will bring:
  • 5+ years' experience within pest control or a closely related sector
  • Experience developing and commercialising regulated products
  • FMCG, consumer products or comparable NPD experience
  • Knowledge of insecticides, rodenticides and pest-control technologies
  • Working knowledge of APVMA requirements and registration pathways
  • Experience managing external manufacturers and technical partners
  • Strong project management, commercial judgement and communication skills
A tertiary qualification in entomology, chemistry, formulation science, biological science or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

Why This Role?
This is a rare opportunity to become the technical specialist behind a new product category within an established consumer business. You’ll have the scope to influence the technical direction, manage the right external partners and see a portfolio move from concept through to products in market.

For someone who knows the pest-control market and enjoys the pace of product commercialisation, there is plenty here to get hold of.

For more information or a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha-Lima on 1300 380 701 or apply via Rimfire Resources.

job.title: Manufacturing Supervisor
job.description:

With local manufacturing at its core, the business values safety, quality workmanship and reliable delivery.

The Opportunity
The Manufacturing Supervisor will support the day-to-day running of the workshop, helping the team complete work safely, efficiently and to the required standard.

This hands-on role suits someone ready to take the next step into supervision. You will help organise priorities, guide the team and resolve routine production issues while remaining involved on the workshop floor.

  • Help plan daily workshop activities and priorities
  • Allocate tasks and follow jobs through to completion
  • Provide practical support and direction to workshop employees
  • Monitor quality, output and delivery timeframes

  • Promote safe work practices and good housekeeping

This role will suit a reliable manufacturing or fabrication professional with some experience guiding others and an interest in developing their supervisory skills.

Why This Role
This is a practical opportunity to step into workshop supervision with the support of an established Australian manufacturer. There are new and exciting changes happening at this company, come and be a part of it.

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at Rimfire Resources. For further information, please contact Mark Turner on 0401 404 451.

job.title: Discharge Supervisor
job.description:
The Company
Fertiglobe is a global leader in nitrogen-based solutions, supplying essential fertilisers that support agriculture and a more sustainable future. In Australia, its integrated manufacturing, blending, storage and distribution network serves major agricultural sectors across the east and southern coasts.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Shipping Manager, the Discharge Supervisor will plan, coordinate and oversee bulk fertiliser vessel discharges across eastern Australia. Based primarily in Port Melbourne, the role combines office-based planning and stakeholder coordination with targeted port attendance to deliver safe, efficient and cost-effective vessel turnarounds.

You will manage discharge plans, schedules, contractors and changing operational conditions. Active discharges require time-sensitive support outside standard hours, including some early mornings, evenings and weekends.
Additional key responsibilities include:
  • Develop discharge plans and monitor vessel movements, port activity and warehouse readiness.
  • Coordinate shipping agents, stevedores, transport providers, warehouse operators and internal teams.
  • Analyse performance, address delays and improve contractor, time and cost outcomes.
  • Maintain oversight of safety, product integrity, environmental obligations and regulatory compliance.
  • Complete operational reporting and attend ports as required.
The Person
We are seeking a commercially minded logistics professional with sound judgement, strong stakeholder skills and a clear focus on safety, service and efficiency.
  • Experience in vessel discharge, port logistics, stevedoring, transport coordination, shipping agency or a related environment.
  • Strong planning, analytical and problem-solving capability.
  • Knowledge of OHS, Chain of Responsibility, maritime safety and environmental compliance.
  • Commercial awareness, attention to detail and confident stakeholder communication.
  • A current driver’s licence and willingness to travel to ports and operational sites.
Why this role?
This newly established role offers genuine ownership of discharge outcomes and the opportunity to improve contractor performance and operational decision-making across Fertiglobe’s Australian supply chain network. Practical onboarding will be provided, with responsibility growing in line with capability.

For further information or an initial confidential discussion, please call Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Manager Governance, Legal and Corporate Services
job.description:
The Company
The Cotton Research and Development Corporation (CRDC) delivers research, development and extension outcomes for Australia’s cotton industry. A partnership between the Commonwealth Government and cotton growers, CRDC invests in world-leading innovation and transformative technologies that benefit growers, the wider industry and regional communities.

Working closely with growers, researchers and innovators, CRDC is ambitious, agile and adaptive, with a strong focus on impact, accountability and continuous improvement.

CRDC offers an exceptional working environment, a genuine passion for the cotton sector and a strong organisational purpose.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Managing Director, the Manager Governance, Legal & Corporate Services provides strategic and operational leadership across CRDC’s governance, legal administration, compliance, policy and corporate services functions. The role supports the Board, Board Committees and Executive, while ensuring governance frameworks, internal controls and organisational processes are current, reliable and effective.

Key areas of responsibility include company secretarial support, Board and Committee administration, contract review, policy management, compliance reporting, HR coordination, risk documentation, supplier arrangements, insurance, asset registers and liaison with external legal, HR and professional advisers.

Specifically, the role will:
  • Maintain and improve governance, compliance and risk frameworks, including legal matters
  • Act as Company Secretary, including statutory compliance, registers, lodgements and governance calendars
  • Coordinate Board and Committee meetings, agendas, papers, minutes, resolutions and actions
  • Review, draft and support negotiation of commercial agreements and contract templates
  • Manage policies, delegations, risk registers, compliance documentation and audit responses
  • Support HR administration, recruitment, onboarding, employment contracts and workplace matters
  • Build organisational capability in governance, contracting and compliance through guidance and training
About You
The successful candidate will be a capable governance, legal or corporate services professional with strong judgement, integrity and the confidence to work with Boards, executives and external advisers.

You will be commercially minded, highly organised and able to balance strategic priorities with hands-on delivery.

Ideally, you will demonstrate:
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in commerce, law, governance and/or business
  • Experience in corporate governance, company secretarial, legal administration or compliance roles
  • Sound understanding of contract administration, risk management and statutory obligations
  • Strong written communication skills suitable for Board and executive documentation
  • Well-developed interpersonal, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience with HR processes, workplace matters and process improvement
  • Experience in a research development corporation, statutory authority or government-funded organisation will be advantageous
Why This Role
This is an opportunity to join a professional, purpose-led organisation that plays an important role in the Australian cotton sector, supporting governance, compliance and corporate services that enable innovation, research and industry impact.

Please apply with your Cover Letter and fresh Resume, or don’t hesitate to call David Jackson on 1300 380 701.

job.title: Accountant - Agribusiness
job.description:
The Company

CHS Broadbent is a leading Australian agribusiness supply chain company with grain marketing, storage, logistics and export operations on the east coast of Australia. CHS Broadbent own and operate grain storage, container packing, and grain freight operations through Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. They are widely recognised by grain producers and markets as leaders in providing reliable, dependable, customer focused service.

The Opportunity

As part of their continued growth, CHS Broadbent are looking for a Accountant to join their Finance team. This role will support the financial control, accounting, reporting and analysis of CHS Broadbent’s grain trading activities, providing independent oversight across commodity positions, grain inventories, mark-to-market valuations, profit and loss reporting, hedging activities and trading exposures.

Working closely with the Trading, Risk, Logistics, Operations and Finance teams, you will support commercial decision-making while ensuring compliance with accounting standards, internal controls and risk management frameworks. The role will be involved in weekly and monthly grain and trading P&L reporting, inventory reconciliations, commodity valuations, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and process improvement initiatives including integration of AI tools and identifying new opportunities and solutions previously not explored.

About You

To be successful in this position you will have:
  • A degree in Accounting, Finance or Commerce, with CPA or CA qualification.
  • Experience in commercial accounting, management accounting, commodity accounting or a related finance role.
  • Strong understanding of inventory reconciliation, financial reporting, P&L analysis and management accounting.
  • Exposure to grain, commodity trading, logistics or agribusiness operations would be highly regarded.
  • Strong analytical capability, attention to detail and confidence working with large volumes of financial and operational data.
  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience using ERP systems, commodity trading platforms, Power Query, Power BI or similar reporting tools beneficial.
  • The ability to partner effectively with trading, operations, logistics, risk and finance stakeholders.
Why This Role

In return, you will be joining an expanding agribusiness with multiple domestic assets and a growing export operation, in a role that provides broad exposure across trading, finance, risk and operations.

If you wish to confidentially discuss this role, please give Ryan Hoiberg or Charlie MacCallum a call on 1300 380 701 or apply now at www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.description:

Its regional Victorian operations combine commercial discipline with a long-term focus on business goals.

The Opportunity
Reporting to a senior operational leader, this role holds overall responsibility for the leadership, management and performance of our client’s operation. Combining strategic oversight with visible, hands-on leadership, you will coordinate people, livestock, land, infrastructure and resources to deliver safe, efficient and sustainable operational outcomes.
  • Develop and deliver annual operating plans, budgets and seasonal work programs across the property.
  • Lead the day-to-day management of production across the property.
  • Oversee herd health, nutrition, genetic improvement, livestock records and animal welfare standards
  • Plan rotational grazing, feed budgets, pasture improvement, fodder production and sustainable land management activities

job.title: General Manager of Supply Chain
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leading, large-scale horticultural business with integrated operations across farming, advanced packing facilities, cold storage, and domestic and export distribution. With a diverse multi-season operating footprint, the business is focused on operational excellence, sustainable produce supply, and continued growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the Chief Commercial Officer, this newly created executive position is based in regional Victoria. As General Manager of Supply Chain, you will own the end-to-end supply chain execution from crop estimate to final customer delivery encompassing fruit storage, packing schedules, procurement and freight.
As a central pillar of the commercial leadership team, you will establish and run a disciplined, binding S&OP / IBP process, bridging farm operations, packing facilities, sales and marketing.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Accountable for the design, cadence, and output of the S&OP / IBP process across all commodities and sites, maintaining a single aligned plan spanning harvest, packing, cold storage and demand.
  • Establishing allocation rules that align crop packout curves with market windows, customer commitments, and packaging formats, while reducing product directed to juice and minimising waste.
  • Owning and managing total cost-to-market per tonne across freight, packaging, dry goods, internal cartage and third-party logistics against budget baselines.
  • Overseeing procurement governance, competitive tender processes, contract registers, rate reviews and supplier performance across major spend categories.
  • Managing domestic and export logistics across sea and air freight, including protocol market compliance (DAFF requirements, orchard and packhouse accreditations and cold chain standards).
  • Managing controlled atmosphere store loading, sealing, release decisions, and container/pallet pooling arrangements to preserve shelf life and outturn quality.
  • Establishing master data governance across core systems, building advanced reporting and decision support capabilities, and elevating the supply chain from reactive execution to a scalable, best-practice operating model.
About You
The ideal candidate will be a commercially astute, data-driven supply chain leader who performs effectively in a fast-paced, seasonal environment and can maintain a clear, evidence-based position when priorities compete or operating pressure increases.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Supply Chain Management, Planning, Business, or an aligned discipline.
  • A minimum of ten years of senior supply chain leadership experience within FMCG, fresh produce, food processing, meat, dairy, or cold-chain environments.
  • Proven experience designing, implementing, and running mature S&OP / IBP processes in a multi-site setting.
  • Deep technical capability across domestic and international logistics, export market protocols, cold-chain management and procurement governance.
  • Strong analytical, data-reconciliation, and critical-thinking skills (proficiency with MS Office and BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau).
  • Outstanding cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence farming, site operations, and commercial sales teams alike.
  • High resilience, adaptability, and an operational focus on continuous improvement and bench-strength building.
Why This Role

We are seeking a practical, technically strong and relationship-driven grains professional who brings:

  • Managing cost-to-serve analysis by sales channel, maintaining license compliance registers, modelling program working capital and assessing counterparty exposure across grower bases.

About You
The ideal candidate will be a commercially astute, CA or CPA qualified finance professional who can translate complex financial information into clear, practical insights for operational leaders.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification with a relevant degree in Accounting, Finance, or Economics.
  • At least five years’ experience, including a minimum of two years in a business partnering role within agricultural, horticultural, food manufacturing or FMCG setting.
  • Proven experience in grower pools, supplier settlement, consignment accounting, or commercial licence and royalty frameworks will be highly regarded.
  • Advanced financial modelling capabilities with the ability to independently build robust 5-year business cases and capital proposals.
  • Demonstrated track record of identifying, quantifying, and delivering cost reduction initiatives, with measurable impact on financial performance.
  • Strong proficiency with Excel, modern ERP/finance systems and business intelligence tools (Power BI, Tableau).
  • Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to constructively challenge operational managers and build collaborative relationships.
Why This Role
This high-visibility role offers direct access to senior leaders and meaningful influence over operational strategy, asset development and value creation across a growing horticultural business. It is an opportunity to combine commercial finance expertise with hands-on operational partnering in a complex, multi-site environment.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701. To apply, visit www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Manager, Digital Agriculture & Artificial Intelligence
job.description:
The Company
Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC) is responsible for planning, investing, and overseeing research, development, and extension for the grains sector in Australia. They meet the evolving needs of grain growers with a vision to be regarded as the grower’s “RD&E department.”

GRDC believes it should be a valued grower asset that is open, transparent, and trusted - a true research partner who seeks to be agile and business like in their operations and improve productivity and profitability for growers.

The Opportunity
GRDC is seeking a Manager - Digital Agriculture & Artificial Intelligence to help shape the future application of digital and AI-enabled technologies across the Australian grains industry.

Working within the Enabling Technologies team, this role focuses on identifying practical opportunities where technology can improve grower decision-making, productivity and industry outcomes. Rather than developing technology directly, the role sits at the intersection of growers, researchers, commercial partners and innovation, helping connect industry challenges with scalable, practical solutions.

You will contribute to the development and management of RD&E investments spanning areas such as precision agriculture, remote sensing, automation, decision-support tools and broader digital agriculture systems. The role combines strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement and commercial awareness to help ensure technologies deliver meaningful value and practical adoption outcomes for Australian grain growers.

This involves:
  • Identifying and developing investment opportunities across digital agriculture and AI enabled systems
  • Developing business cases and investment proposals with clear return-on-investment rationale
  • Managing RD&E investments, including milestones, risk, budget and contract performance
  • Supporting adoption and path-to-market strategies for emerging technologies and project outputs
  • Building strong networks across industry, research, government and commercial stakeholders
  • Providing strategic input across broader GRDC investment portfolios
  • Supporting collaboration between researchers, growers and industry stakeholders
  • Contributing to technology deployment across agronomy, farming systems, biosecurity and crop improvement programs
About You
To be successful in this influential role you will have:
  • Experience within digital agriculture, agtech, precision agriculture, agricultural innovation or related sectors
  • Strong communication and relationship-building capability across researchers, growers, commercial partners and industry stakeholders
  • The ability to understand complex technical concepts and translate them into practical industry outcomes
  • Commercial awareness and the ability to assess opportunities through both technical and grower adoption lenses
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, combined with curiosity and initiative
  • Experience contributing to RD&E projects, innovation programs or technology-focused initiatives within agriculture or adjacent sectors
  • A collaborative and adaptable working style
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in agriculture, plant science, science, engineering, data science or related disciplines
  • Experience within Australian broadacre or grains production systems (highly regarded)
Importantly, GRDC is seeking someone who combines curiosity, commercial thinking and strong stakeholder engagement with a genuine interest in the future of digital agriculture. You’ll play a key role in helping emerging technologies deliver practical value for Australian grain growers.

The role involves periodic travel to engage with growers, researchers and industry stakeholders across Australia’s grain-growing regions. Full Australian Working Rights (Citizenship or Permanent Residency) are required.

Why This Role
  • Help shape how digital agriculture is applied across the Australian grains industry
  • High-impact role bridging technology, industry and practical grower outcomes
  • Opportunity to grow into broader strategic leadership responsibilities over time
  • Collaborative team environment with strong industry exposure and flexibility
For confidential enquiries and a copy of the Position Description, please call Marcela Rocha Lima on 1300 380 701 or apply via rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Lead Production Agronomist
job.description:
The Company
GenTech Seeds is a recognised premium brand in Australian agribusiness and the exclusive producer and distributor of Pioneer® brand products in Australia.

The business works closely with growers to produce hybrid seed products suited to Australian farming systems, with a major seed manufacturing and distribution site based at Narromine in Central West NSW. The Narromine site brings together production, quality, field operations and distribution within a highly seasonal seed production environment.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Site Manager, this role will lead technical agronomy across commercial seed production in the Macquarie Valley.

The role is focused on corn through summer and canola through winter, with some involvement in sorghum, production trials and broader improvement projects. It combines crop agronomy, grower engagement and close collaboration with production, field and quality teams.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Manage seasonal agronomy programs across corn, canola and sorghum seed production.
  • Support growers with crop establishment, nutrition, irrigation, pest and disease decisions.
  • Monitor crop performance, seasonal risk, yield potential and seed quality requirements.
  • Contribute to production planning, trials and continuous improvement projects.
Seed production experience would be valuable, but the business is open to experienced agronomists from broader broadacre, row crop or production backgrounds who can bring technical depth, sound judgement and the right team approach.

About You
You are a practical agronomist who enjoys being close to the crop, the grower and the commercial outcome.

Experience in corn, canola or seed production would be valuable, although sound crop agronomy, good judgement and grower communication will be the key.

You will bring:
  • Agronomy experience across broadacre, irrigated or seed production systems.
  • Confidence working directly with growers, contractors and operational teams.
  • Sound judgement across crop performance, timing, quality and seasonal risk.
  • A hands-on, accountable approach with the ability to take ownership of a region.
Why This Role?
This is a genuine opportunity to step into a senior agronomy role with clear ownership of a key production region. You will be close to the decisions that affect crop performance, seed quality and grower outcomes, while working within a respected national business with strong systems, established grower relationships and a premium brand in the market.

For someone who enjoys technical agronomy, commercial production and building trust with growers, this role offers the chance to have real influence across a high-value seed production program.

How to Apply
For a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha Lima on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Regional Manager - Goondiwindi
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leader in providing science based, agricultural field research services, conducting trials in the major broadacre and horticultural cropping regions of Australia. With offices and staff strategically positioned, providing a full suite of services, they are focussed on helping advance new technologies to market and developing new agricultural inputs and systems.

With experienced staff and working with leading edge technology, business is based on creating great relationships with clients, so they are committed to open and consistent communication.

The role
A new role has been created for a Regional Manager - Goondiwindi to manage an area of the northern business research unit, overseeing the field operations and logistics in the broadacre regions of Northern NSW, Sth West QLD and Central QLD.

Reporting to the Northern Business Manager, you will be responsible for managerial, technical and administrative areas of the unit’s business performance. This includes working closely with your team of 7 direct reports to ensure delivery of clients and trial objectives. The research work is comprehensive and diverse covering a wide range of crops across residue, efficacy and breeding trials.  It is estimated that 60% of your time would be in the office and 40% in the field, which would include training newer staff and running your own small field trial program.

There is a requirement to travel at regular intervals to the regional offices.

The Person
The successful person will have the following skills and attributes:
  • Commercial business & people management experience
  • Agronomy knowledge and familiarity with crops grown in this geographic region
  • Ideally field trial (R&D) and logistics experience, with good attention to detail
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Agriculture/ Business /Commerce
A generous salary package including vehicle is on offer for the successful candidate. There is some flexibility on location however you are required to work closely with the teams in Goondiwindi and Narrabri.

You may have local industry experience in crop protection, seed, retail distribution, research or Research Development Corporations (RDC’s), and looking for a new challenge to step up into a leadership role.

Come and join a leading research agribusiness bringing your business and people management skills. The skilled and dynamic team is growing, accumulating a wealth of experience, providing learning opportunities around the country.

Please call Al Kellaway on 1300 380 701 for a discussion and copy of the Position Description, or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au.
